title: The model is one stage of the request
caption: A request travels ingress, parse, preprocess, batch, execute, postprocess and dispatch — each stage adds latency and a queue. The forward pass is one term of the budget.

title: Little's Law sizes the resident population
caption: At 1,000 arrivals per second and a 50 ms mean time in system, ~50 requests live inside the service at once. Buffers, threads and accelerator memory are sized by that population.

title: A batch window is spent waiting before it executes
caption: Requests trickle in over the formation window; the batch latency everyone quotes starts only after the window fills. Early arrivals pay the whole formation delay.

title: The serving plan, end to end
caption: Traffic sets the resident population (Little's Law), utilization sets the tail (the knee), the window trades formation delay for batch throughput, and replicas plus headroom carry the peak.

title: Waiting near saturation
caption: In a single-server M/M/1 queue, mean time in system divided by mean service time is 1/(1 − utilization). Moving from 80% to 90% load doubles the multiplier from 5× to 10×. The next five percentage points double it again. At a balanced peak of 1,000 requests/s and 285 requests/s per replica, four replicas run at 88% and five at 70%. Five is the candidate to load-test. Measure request p99 on peak traffic to verify the deadline.
